observation.visible_scene: A left hand holds a reflective optical disc (CD/DVD) by its left edge, tilting it toward the camera inside a light box with a red backdrop and white reflective side panels. Below the disc lie a folded blue cloth and a small beige clay/putty piece. In the upper-right background sits a small black desk fan with a blue grille and visible blades.
visible_changes: The hand continuously tilts and re-angles the disc, rocking it so the disc face alternates between a more upright and a more laid-back orientation; the disc's center stays roughly fixed in the frame.

As the disc's tilt changes, the iridescent diffraction pattern shifts across its surface: a rainbow 'fan' of colors moves from the lower half (e.g. frames 1, 10, 31) to the upper half (e.g. frames 4, 20, 24) and back, and bright rectangular light reflections slide around the disc.
The fan blades in the background show motion consistent with rotation while the fan housing itself remains stationary.
The blue cloth and the beige clay piece do not move; the hand, disc, and background fan keep their relative positions.
The camera framing is essentially static (background panels and fan hold constant positions), so the observed changes are due to the hand tilting the disc, not camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: The purpose of the clay piece and the cloth, and any action performed with them outside this excerpt.
Whether the disc is being spun about its own axis or only tilted; the excerpt shows tilting.
What precedes or follows this segment.
uncertain_details: Exact rotation speed or direction of the fan blades (only blur is visible).
Whether there is a slight overall rotation of the disc in addition to the tilt; the dominant visible change is tilt-induced reflection shift.
Fine hand movements are partly occluded by the disc itself.
